answer_1.quote: Large Language Models (LLMs) have become the new norm in many downstream NLP tasks. In utilizing these LLMs, Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting is found to improve performances for tasks that require complex reasoning, such as math word problems, commonsense reasoning, and symbolic manipulation.
answer_1.outputs: The model generates reasoning chains (CoTs) and final answers for question-answering and fact verification tasks, which are then post-edited using external knowledge retrieval to improve factual correctness and accuracy.

answer_2.quote: Reported in Table , we observe that CoT improves on top of the Standard few-shot setting. CoT-SC, on the other hand, does not demonstrate a good improvement on the baseline. Using the calibrator from , AUC is improved as it learns to calibrate the answer weights based on ground-truth contexts provided in the dataset.

answer_4.quote: To closely examine the faithfulness of the generated reasoning chains, we also conduct a small-scale human study experiment. During the experiment, two human volunteers are shown 50 randomly selected questions with generated reasoning chains from CoT-SC and Verify-and-Edit on the HotpotQA dataset. They are then asked to select the more factually consistent one.
answer_4.guideline: Volunteers are encouraged to use search engines as assistance. They are asked to select the more factually consistent reasoning chain between CoT-SC and Verify-and-Edit.
